summary:
**ASTRA-CORE: Predictive Astronaut Health Intelligence Prototype**

Developed by Team Anvils, ASTRA-CORE is a lightweight, AI-powered health-monitoring prototype designed to demonstrate predictive health intelligence for deep space missions. Operating as a unified medical support system, it integrates five core capabilities: a real-time Health Dashboard for vital signs, continuous AI Health Analysis to detect anomalies against personalized baselines, a visual Digital Health Twin mapping historical and simulated trends, an AI Medical Assistant providing protocol-based guidance, and an Interactive Emergency Simulator.

To maximize demonstration impact while minimizing backend complexity, the MVP utilizes predefined synthetic astronaut data and a Lovable-generated interface, eliminating the need for physical sensors. Rather than disconnected screens, ASTRA-CORE features a single connected workflow where triggering a simulated emergency dynamically updates the dashboard, risk analysis, and digital twin concurrently. By merging continuous physiological monitoring with predictive AI, ASTRA-CORE establishes a conceptual foundation for next-generation crew health systems, equipping mission control and onboard medical officers with an intuitive tool to ensure astronaut safety during prolonged spaceflight.
details:
Introduction Team Anvils is proud to present ASTRA-CORE, a lightweight, AI-powered predictive astronaut health intelligence prototype developed for deep space exploration. As missions push humanity further from Earth, ensuring the physiological safety of crew members without immediate mission control intervention is a critical challenge. ASTRA-CORE addresses this by transforming complex medical telemetry into an intuitive, autonomous digital twin system. Below is a detailed overview of our prototype's functionality, impact, and the technical approach we took to build it.

What it does and how it works ASTRA-CORE is a lightweight, AI-powered predictive health intelligence prototype designed for deep space missions. It functions as a unified medical support system that ingests simulated astronaut telemetry (heart rate, blood oxygen, body temperature, sleep, and physical activity) to establish a personalized health baseline. The system operates through a single connected workflow consisting of five core features:

  • Centralized Dashboard: Displays real-time vital signs and the astronaut's profile.
  • AI Health Analysis: Continuously monitors data to detect anomalies and deviations from the astronaut's baseline.
  • Digital Health Twin: Visually maps the astronaut's current health status and historical trends.
  • AI Medical Assistant: Acts as a virtual medical officer that explains detected anomalies in plain language and outputs actionable, protocol-based guidance.
  • Interactive Emergency Simulator: Allows users to manually trigger predefined abnormal health events. When triggered, the system dynamically updates the dashboard, digital twin, and risk analysis concurrently to demonstrate the end-to-end detection and alert process.

Benefits of the project ASTRA-CORE centralizes complex medical data into an accessible, highly visual format. By combining continuous physiological monitoring with predictive AI, it shifts the focus of space medicine from reactive treatment to proactive prevention. The system's ability to autonomously analyze anomalies and provide protocol-driven guidance is especially beneficial for deep space missions where communication latency with Earth makes immediate medical support from mission control impossible.

Intended impact The project is designed to set a conceptual foundation for next-generation crew health systems. Its intended impact is to ensure astronaut safety during prolonged spaceflight (such as Mars missions) by equipping both onboard medical officers and remote mission control with an intuitive, autonomous tool that reduces cognitive load during high-stress medical emergencies.

Tools, coding languages, and software used To maximize demonstration impact while minimizing backend complexity within the hackathon timeframe, our team utilized the following stack:

  • UI/UX & Prototyping: Lovable was used to rapidly generate the interactive frontend interface and unified workflows. Figma was used for initial wireframing and design layouts.
  • Frontend Development: React.js and Tailwind CSS to render the dynamic dashboard and Digital Health Twin interface.
  • Backend & Data: Python was utilized to structure the logic for the AI Health Analysis and Medical Assistant.
  • Data Infrastructure: The system relies entirely on predefined synthetic astronaut data (JSON formatting) to drive the emergency simulations, intentionally omitting the need for physical sensors or complex hardware integrations for the MVP.

How the project is creative Instead of presenting a traditional slideshow of disconnected static screens, ASTRA-CORE's creativity lies in its Connected Demonstration Workflow. By integrating an Emergency Simulator directly into the prototype, we created a single, unified loop. When a judge or user triggers a sample health scenario, they watch the dashboard numbers spike, the Digital Twin light up with risk indicators, and the AI Medical Assistant instantly generate a diagnostic report all at the exact same time. This creates a highly convincing, high-fidelity representation of a final integrated system without requiring a massive backend.

Factors Team Anvils considered

  • Demonstrability vs. Complexity: We recognized that building a real-time medical backend was impossible for a hackathon. We purposefully constrained our MVP scope to one astronaut profile and synthetic data so we could focus on the user experience and the seamless interaction between the AI
